title: Low-Calorie Double Smash Cheeseburger
summary: Two thin smashed patties of 96% lean beef with one slice of American cheese, dill pickle planks and paper-thin rinsed onion on a toasted bun, with a light mayo, mustard and Sriracha sauce.
notes: Video: 'The Best Low Calorie Burger Ever' on the Joshua Weissman Recipes channel (UCUAg71CJEvFdOnujmep1Svw). Written recipe for the same dish: https://www.joshuaweissman.com/recipes/easy-healthy-high-protein-cheeseburger-recipe (serves 4, prep 3 min, cook 5 min; it publishes 450 kcal, 15 g fat, 45 g protein, 44 g carbs per burger; the video says 33 g carbs). The video states the sauce, the beef (1.5 lb, eight 3 oz balls, two per burger), one cheese slice per burger, and the bun (Dave's Killer Bread 'Burger Buns Done Right', 160 kcal each). From the written recipe: 2 large dill pickles and 1/2 sweet onion. He uses 96% lean beef; USDA's closest raw record is 95% lean. The bun weight is our estimate: 60 g each makes the USDA whole-wheat bun about 160 kcal, matching what he says. Salt (1 tsp kosher) and pepper on the patties are our estimates; salt and pepper in the sauce are not counted.

steps.text: Whisk the light mayo, mustard, Sriracha, salt and pepper. This is enough for four burgers.
Slice the pickles lengthwise into planks a little under 1/4 inch thick.
Slice the onion paper-thin (a mandoline helps), then rinse in cold water, ideally with ice, and drain well.
Weigh the beef into eight 3 oz portions and roll them into tight, even balls.
Toast the buns dry on both sides over medium heat, about 2 minutes, without butter.
On a very hot, well-seasoned griddle or nonstick pan over medium-high heat, smash each ball under parchment to about 25% wider than the bun. Season with salt and pepper.
Flip early, when the patty is about two-thirds cooked, so the lean beef stays juicy. Put one slice of cheese on one patty per burger; cook 1-2 minutes per side at most.
Stack two patties per burger. Build: sauced bottom bun, pickles, onion, the cheesy double patty, and about a tablespoon of sauce on the top bun.
